name: Concealed recognition

intent.purpose: Establish the shared space and the stranger's concealed hands before the reveal.
intent.reason: The audience needs the ordinary setup and the gloves registered before the scar can land.
intent.attention: The gloved hands, then the reaching motion.
intent.relationships: Two strangers in neutral, enforced proximity.

staging.positions: Ada and the stranger sit opposite each other across the seats.
staging.facing: Both face each other in profile to camera.
staging.eyelines: Ada's gaze is casual, not yet fixed on him.
staging.movement: The stranger reaches into his coat and brings his hand forward with the ticket.
staging.camera: Static profile two-shot at seated eye level.

editorial.cutOut: Cut on the reaching action to the insert of the wrist.
editorial.timing: Unhurried, letting the quiet settle before the reveal.

advanced.continuity: Gloves are on both hands. The ticket emerges from his coat.
advanced.assumptions: The profile axis and window side are staging choices.

shots.title: Strangers Across the Carriage
shots.sourceExcerpt: Ada sits opposite a stranger whose gloves hide his hands. He reaches for his ticket, exposing a crescent scar. Ada recognises it but keeps her expression calm.
shots.description: Opening: a wide-medium profile two-shot down the carriage. Ada sits on one side and the stranger sits opposite, the dark night window streaking between and beside them. His gloved hands rest visibly in his lap. The camera holds steady with only a slight train sway. The stranger shifts and reaches into his coat for his ticket, and his gloved hand begins to come forward. Ending: the two-shot, with his hand extending toward the space between them.
shots.atmosphere: Dim night carriage, rhythmic rail clatter, passing lights flickering across the window.
shots.music: None, or a barely audible low drone.

intent.purpose: Reveal the scar as the scene's key information.
intent.reason: The audience must see exactly what Ada sees.
intent.relationships: His unguarded moment becomes her knowledge.

staging.movement: The cuff slips back as his hand extends.
staging.camera: Close insert, roughly matching Ada's eyeline.

editorial.cutIn: Matched on the stranger's reaching action from the two-shot.
editorial.cutOut: Cut to Ada's reaction to the scar.
editorial.timing: Brief, just long enough to read the shape.

advanced.continuity: Same hand and ticket as the previous shot.
advanced.assumptions: The scar is on the wrist where the glove ends. The script states only that reaching exposes it.

shots.title: The Crescent Scar
shots.sourceExcerpt: Ada sits opposite a stranger whose gloves hide his hands. He reaches for his ticket, exposing a crescent scar. Ada recognises it but keeps her expression calm.
shots.description: Opening: a tight insert on the stranger's gloved hand holding the ticket, roughly from Ada's seated vantage. As he extends the ticket, the glove's cuff slides back and exposes a crescent-shaped scar on his skin. Ending: the scar clearly framed beside the ticket.
shots.atmosphere: Rail clatter continues, and window light passes over the skin.
shots.music: A subtle sting or a held tone as the scar is revealed.

intent.purpose: Show Ada's recognition and her controlled concealment of it.
intent.reason: The audience shares her secret while seeing that she hides it.
intent.attention: Her eyes against her still expression.
intent.relationships: Ada now holds knowledge the stranger does not know she has.

staging.eyelines: First down toward his hand, then level toward him.
staging.camera: Static tight close-up from the stranger's side of the axis.

editorial.cutOut: Cut to the stranger as he speaks.

advanced.continuity: Ada keeps her eyeline consistent with the stranger's opposite position.

shots.title: Ada Recognises
shots.sourceExcerpt: Ada sits opposite a stranger whose gloves hide his hands. He reaches for his ticket, exposing a crescent scar. Ada recognises it but keeps her expression calm.
shots.description: Opening: a tight close-up of Ada, her eyes lowered toward his hand. Recognition flickers in her eyes, but her face stays composed and calm. She lifts her gaze back to neutral. Ending: Ada's calm close-up with her eyes level.
shots.atmosphere: Flickering window light across her face, steady rail rhythm.

intent.reason: The question raises the stakes. Has he noticed something?
intent.attention: The stranger's face and his ambiguous intent.
intent.relationships: He tests the familiarity, and Ada sits in the foreground under scrutiny.

staging.positions: Ada's shoulder is in the foreground and the stranger is opposite.
staging.eyelines: The stranger looks directly at Ada.

editorial.cutIn: Cut on the start of his line after Ada's held reaction.
editorial.cutOut: Cut to Ada for her answer.
editorial.timing: Tight, with the line landing quickly.

advanced.continuity: The ticket remains in his gloved hand. Screen direction matches Ada's eyeline.

shots.title: Have We Met?
shots.description: Opening: over Ada's shoulder, a medium close-up of the stranger facing her, his gloved hand with the ticket still between them. He studies her and asks his question. Ending: the stranger holding his look, waiting for her answer.
shots.atmosphere: Quiet carriage, rail rhythm under the line.

intent.purpose: Show Ada deflecting with a loaded line, then quietly withholding her ticket.
intent.reason: Her words and her action together show concealment and quiet defiance.
intent.attention: Her calm delivery, then the ticket disappearing into her coat.
intent.relationships: Ada asserts control while keeping her secret.

staging.eyelines: Ada holds her gaze on the stranger throughout.
staging.movement: Her hand moves the ticket into her coat.
staging.camera: Static medium single framed to include her hands.

editorial.cutIn: Cut for Ada's answer to his question.
editorial.cutOut: Scene end on her held look.
editorial.timing: Measured, with a pause after the line before the ticket action.

advanced.continuity: Ada's ticket is introduced here from her hand or lap. Her coat is on.
advanced.assumptions: Where her ticket starts is not specified in the script.

shots.title: I Would Remember
shots.sourceExcerpt:
### ADA

I would remember.

She slips her own ticket into her coat instead of handing it to him.
shots.description: Opening: a medium single of Ada from the stranger's side, wider than her earlier close-up so that her coat and hands are in frame. She answers evenly. Then, keeping her eyes on him, she slips her own ticket into her coat instead of handing it to him. Ending: Ada composed, her hand withdrawing from her coat, her gaze level on the stranger.
shots.atmosphere: Window light continues to pass, rail rhythm steady, tension unresolved.
shots.music: The low drone returns faintly, unresolved.

strategies.dramaticProgression: A neutral encounter between strangers turns into a private recognition. Ada sees the scar, conceals what she knows, deflects his question, and quietly withholds her ticket. The tension is in her controlled surface over hidden knowledge.
strategies.visualProgression: The scene opens on a balanced two-shot of shared, ordinary space. A tight insert isolates the scar as the revelation. Coverage then narrows to Ada's guarded close-up, moves to an over-the-shoulder on the stranger for his probing question, and ends on a single of Ada whose frame includes her concealing hand.
strategies.audienceInformation: The audience sees the scar and Ada's recognition, which the stranger does not register. The audience does not learn what the scar means to her or who he is. That gap drives suspense.
strategies.spatialAnchors: Ada and the stranger sit facing each other across the carriage seats. The night window runs beside them. His gloved hands and the ticket are between them. Ada's coat is on her side. Exact seat sides and window position are staging assumptions.
